items.title: A U-admissible blowup makes the strict transform flat and of finite presentation, for an over-S scheme flat over a quasi-compact open U and of finite type over S
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for X -> S of finite type and quasi-separated whose restriction to a quasi-compact open U is flat and locally of finite presentation, some U-admissible blowup S' -> S has strict transform flat and of finite presentation over S' (statement lines 9122-9135). The proof is a reduction: strict transforms remain quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so local finite presentation may be proved first; a finite affine open cover X = W_1 union ... union W_n allows the conclusion for X to be assembled from the conclusions for the W_i once a U-admissible blowup dominating all of them is chosen, using the existence of a common refinement of admissible blowups; and for affine X one embeds X as a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open V of A^n_S and applies the flattening theorem to the pushforward i_*O_X, then uses that strict transform commutes with pushforward along an affine morphism, which converts flatness of the strict transform of i_*O_X into flatness of i'_*O_{X'} and hence of X' over S' (proof lines 9138-9169). The choice of the ambient affine space, the use of the flattening theorem on a pushforward rather than on X itself, and the strict-transform-commutes-with-pushforward step are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
